title.zh: 卷一百三十一 列傳第六十九: 宦者 梁珫 宋珪 潘守恆 方伎 劉完素 張從正 李慶嗣 紀天錫 張元素 馬貴中 武禎子:亢 李懋 胡德新
title.en: Volume 131 Biographies 69: Huan Zhe, Liang Chong, Song Gui, Pan Shouheng, Fang Ji, Liu Wansu, Zhang Congzheng, Li Qingsi, Ji Tianxi, Zhang Yuansu, Ma Guizhong, Wu Zhen son: Kang, Li Mao, Hu Dexin
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 列傳第六十九: 宦者 梁珫 宋珪 潘守恆 方伎 劉完素 張從正 李慶嗣 紀天錫 張元素 馬貴中 武禎子:亢 李懋 胡德新 Volume 131 Biographies 69: Huan Zhe, Liang Chong, Song Gui, Pan Shouheng, Fang Ji, Liu Wansu, Zhang Congzheng, Li Qingsi, Ji Tianxi, Zhang Yuansu, Ma Guizhong, Wu Zhen son: Kang, Li Mao, Hu Dexin

sentences.zh: 古之宦者皆出於刑人，刑余不可列於士庶，故掌宮寺之事，謂之「婦寺」焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity all eunuchs came from punished men; those mutilated by punishment could not be ranked among gentlemen and commoners, so they managed palace and temple affairs and were called 'palace women attendants.'
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times every eunuch was drawn from the ranks of criminals. Once mutilated by penal law, a man could no longer stand among scholars or the common people, and so he was put in charge of palace affairs — hence the term "palace women attendants."

sentences.zh: 東漢以來，宦者養子以繼世。

translations.literal: From the Eastern Han onward, eunuchs adopted sons to continue their lineages.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Han dynasty on, eunuchs adopted sons to carry on their family lines.

sentences.zh: 唐世，繼者皆為閹人，其初進也，性多巧慧便僻、善固恩寵，及其得志，黨比糾結不可制。

translations.literal: In the Tang age, successors were all castrated men; when they first entered service, their natures were mostly clever, artful, and devious, skilled at securing favor, and once they gained their aims, factional cliques formed and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, every successor was a castrated man. On first entering court they were apt to be clever, pliant, and devious, expert at holding imperial favor; once they rose to power, their factions knotted together beyond restraint.

sentences.zh: 東漢以宦者亡，唐又甚焉。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han perished because of eunuchs, and the Tang suffered even more severely.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han fell to ruin through eunuchs, and the Tang suffered even worse.

sentences.zh: 世儒論宦者之害，如毒藥猛虎之不可拯也。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars of the age spoke of the harm of eunuchs as poison or a fierce tiger that cannot be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of the age described the harm done by eunuchs as beyond remedy — like poison or a ravening tiger.

sentences.zh: 金法置近侍局，嘗與政事，而宦者少與焉。

translations.literal: Under Jin law the Imperial Attendants Bureau was established and at times took part in government affairs, but eunuchs had little share in it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin institutions set up the Imperial Attendants Bureau, which at times handled state affairs, yet eunuchs seldom had a role in it.

sentences.zh: 惟海陵時有梁珫，章宗時有梁道、李新喜幹政，二君為所誤多矣。

translations.literal: Only under Hailing there was Liang Chong, and under Zhangzong there were Liang Dao and Li Xinxi meddling in government; both rulers were greatly misled by them.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Emperor Hailing did Liang Chong, and under Emperor Zhangzong did Liang Dao and Li Xinxi, meddle in government — and both sovereigns were led badly astray.

sentences.zh: 世傳梁道勸章宗納李妃後宮，金史不載梁道始末，弗得而論次之。

translations.literal: Popular tradition says Liang Dao urged Zhangzong to take Consort Li into the inner palace; the History of Jin does not record Liang Dao's beginning and end, so he cannot be arranged in narrative order.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that Liang Dao persuaded Zhangzong to take Consort Li into the harem, but the History of Jin does not record Liang Dao's full story, so his career cannot be set out here in proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 惟宋珪、潘守恆頗能諷諫宣、哀，時有裨益，蓋傭之佼佼、鐵之錚錚者也。

translations.literal: Only Song Gui and Pan Shouheng were fairly able to remonstrate with the Xuande and Aizong emperors and at times were of benefit — outstanding among hirelings, ringing like iron.
translations.idiomatic: Only Song Gui and Pan Shouheng could remonstrate with Emperors Xuanzong and Aizong with real effect, and at times they did genuine good — the finest among servants, ringing true as tempered iron.

sentences.zh: 作《宦者傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the 'Biographies of Eunuchs' was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence these biographies of eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 梁珫，本大抃家奴，隨元妃入宮，以閹豎事海陵。

translations.literal: Liang Chong was originally a household slave of the Daban family; he entered the palace with the primary consort and served Hailing as a castrated attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chong had been a bondservant in the household of Daban. He entered the palace with the primary consort and served Emperor Hailing as a eunuch attendant.

sentences.zh: 珫性便佞，善迎合，特見寵信，舊制，宦者惟掌掖廷宮闈之事。

translations.literal: Chong's nature was facile and sycophantic; he was skilled at flattery and received special favor and trust. Under the old system eunuchs managed only the inner palace and women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was smooth and obsequious by nature, adept at currying favor, and won exceptional trust. By longstanding custom eunuchs had managed only the inner palace and the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，始以王光道為內藏庫使，衛愈、梁安仁皆以宦官領內藏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande, Wang Guangdao was first made director of the Inner Treasury, and Wei Yu and Liang Anren likewise were eunuchs placed over the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande (1151), Wang Guangdao became the first director of the Inner Treasury; Wei Yu and Liang Anren were also eunuchs put in charge of the imperial storehouses.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂光道等曰：「人言宦者不可用，朕以為不然。

translations.literal: Hailing said to Guangdao and the others: 'People say eunuchs cannot be employed; I do not think so.'
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told Guangdao and the others, "People say eunuchs should never be used. I disagree.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗委張承業以軍，竟立大功，此中豈無人乎。

translations.literal: Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entrusted Zhang Chengye with armies and he in the end achieved great merit — are there not capable men among them?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang entrusted Zhang Chengye with his armies, and Zhang won great merit in the end. Surely capable men can be found among them as well.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜悉此意。

translations.literal: You should all fully grasp this intent.
translations.idiomatic: You must take this to heart.

sentences.zh: 帑藏之物皆出民力，費十致一，當糾察奸弊，犯者必罰無赦。

translations.literal: Treasury goods all come from the people's labor; ten parts are spent to deliver one — you must investigate corruption and malfeasance, and offenders must be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Everything in the treasury comes from the people's labor — ten parts spent for every one received. Root out fraud and abuse; anyone who offends will be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 」宦者始與政事，而珫委任尤甚，累官近侍局使。

translations.literal: ' Eunuchs began to take part in government affairs, and Chong was entrusted above all others, rising through offices to become director of the Imperial Attendants Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on eunuchs entered state affairs, and Chong was entrusted above all the rest, eventually rising to director of the Imperial Attendants Bureau.

sentences.zh: 及營建南京宮室，海陵數數使珫往視工役。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital palace was being built, Hailing repeatedly sent Chong to inspect the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital palace was under construction, Hailing sent Chong again and again to inspect the work.

sentences.zh: 是時，一殿之費已不可勝計，珫或言其未善，即盡撒去。

translations.literal: At that time the cost of a single hall was already beyond reckoning; if Chong sometimes said it was not good enough, everything was torn down.
translations.idiomatic: By then the cost of a single hall was beyond counting. If Chong said the work was not good enough, the whole structure was torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 雖丞相張浩亦曲意事之，與之均禮。

translations.literal: Even Chief Councillor Zhang Hao bent his will to serve him and treated him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Even Chief Councillor Zhang Hao humored him and treated him as an equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 海陵欲伐宋，珫因極言宋劉貴妃絕色傾國。

translations.literal: When Hailing wished to attack Song, Chong therefore spoke at length of how Consort Liu of Song was of peerless beauty that could overturn a state.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing planned to attack the Song, Chong lavished praise on Consort Liu of Song, declaring her beauty unmatched and enough to topple a kingdom.

sentences.zh: 海陵大喜，及南征將行，命縣君高師姑兒貯衾褥之新潔者俟得劉貴妃用之。

translations.literal: Hailing was greatly pleased, and when the southern campaign was about to set out he ordered the county lady Gao Shigu'er to store fresh, clean bedding to await use when Consort Liu was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was delighted. As the southern campaign was about to begin, he ordered the county lady Gao Shigu'er to lay aside fresh, clean bedding for the day when Consort Liu would be his.

sentences.zh: 議者言珫與宋通謀，勸帝伐宋，征天下兵以疲弊中國。

translations.literal: Critics said Chong conspired with Song, urging the emperor to attack Song and levy troops from across the realm to exhaust and weaken China.
translations.idiomatic: Some charged that Chong was in league with the Song: he had urged the emperor to invade so that armies raised across the empire would wear China down.

sentences.zh: 海陵至和州，聞珫與宋人交通有狀，謂珫曰：「聞汝與宋國交通，傳泄事情。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached He Prefecture he heard that there was substance to Chong's dealings with Song men, and said to Chong: 'I hear you have dealings with the Song state and leak affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached He Prefecture he learned that Chong's traffic with the Song was well founded. He said to Chong, "I hear you have been dealing with the Song and leaking our affairs.

sentences.zh: 汝本奴隸，朕拔擢至此，乃敢爾耶。

translations.literal: You were originally a slave; I raised you to this position — how dare you act thus?
translations.idiomatic: You were a slave. I raised you to this height — and you dare do this?

sentences.zh: 若至江南詢得實跡，殺汝亦未晚也。

translations.literal: If when we reach Jiangnan inquiry confirms the facts, killing you will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If inquiry south of the Yangzi confirms it, your execution will not come a day too soon.

sentences.zh: 」又謂校書郎田與信曰：「爾面目亦可疑，必與珫同謀者。

translations.literal: ' He also said to the proofreader Tian Yuxin: 'Your face too is suspicious; you must be Chong's co-conspirator.'
translations.idiomatic: " He told the proofreader Tian Yuxin, "Your face is suspicious too. You must be Chong's accomplice.

sentences.zh: 」皆命執於軍中。

translations.literal: ' He ordered both seized in the army.
translations.idiomatic: " Both were ordered seized in the camp.

sentences.zh: 海陵遇弑，珫、與信皆為亂軍所殺。

translations.literal: When Hailing met assassination, Chong and Yuxin were both killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was assassinated, Chong and Yuxin were both killed by the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 宋珪，本名乞奴，燕人也。

translations.literal: Song Gui, original name Qinu, was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gui, born Qinu, was from the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 為內侍殿頭。

translations.literal: He served as head of the inner attendants' hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served as head attendant in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗以元夕欲觀燈戲，命乞奴監作，乞奴誶語雲：「社稷棄之中都，南京作燈戲有何看耶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once on the Lantern Festival wished to watch lantern plays and ordered Qinu to supervise their production; Qinu cursed, saying: 'The altars of state were abandoned at the Central Capital — what is there to see in lantern plays at the Southern Capital?'
translations.idiomatic: On one Lantern Festival Emperor Xuanzong wished to watch lantern plays and ordered Qinu to oversee them. Qinu swore aloud: "The realm was abandoned at the Central Capital — what is there to watch in lantern plays at the Southern Capital?"

sentences.zh: 」宣宗微聞之，杖之二十，既而悔之，有旨宣諭。

translations.literal: ' Xuanzong faintly heard of it and had him beaten twenty strokes; afterward he regretted it and issued an edict of reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong caught wind of it and had him beaten twenty strokes, then regretted it and sent an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 哀宗放鷂後苑，鷂逸去，敕近侍追訪之，市中一農民臂此鷂，近侍不敢言宮中所逸者，百方索之，農民不與，與之物直，僅乃得。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong released a hawk in the rear park and it escaped; he ordered attendants to track it down. In the market a farmer had the hawk on his arm; the attendants dared not say it was the palace bird that had escaped and tried every means to obtain it; the farmer would not give it up until they paid its price and barely then obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong released a hawk in the rear park and it escaped. He ordered attendants to find it. In the market a farmer had the bird on his arm. The attendants dared not say it was the palace hawk; they tried every approach, but the farmer would not yield until they paid him its price — and only then did they get it back.

sentences.zh: 事聞，哀宗欲送其人於有司，乞奴從旁諫曰：「貴畜賤人，豈可宣示四方。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, Aizong wished to hand the man over to the authorities; Qinu remonstrated from the side, saying: 'To value beasts and slight men — how can that be displayed to the four quarters?'
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, Aizong meant to hand the farmer over to the authorities. Qinu remonstrated at his side: "To prize a bird and slight a man — how can we show that to the world?"

sentences.zh: 」哀宗惡其大訐，又仗之，尋亦悔，賜物慰遣之。

translations.literal: ' Aizong disliked his bold remonstrance and had him beaten again; soon he regretted it too and bestowed goods to comfort and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: " Aizong disliked the blunt rebuke and had him beaten again. Soon he regretted that as well and sent gifts to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗至歸德，馬軍元帥蒲察官奴為變，殺左丞李蹊、參政石盞女魯歡以下從官三百餘人。

translations.literal: When Aizong reached Guide, the cavalry marshal Pucha Guannu mutinied and killed Left Vice Councillor Li Xi, Participating Councillor Shizhan Nuluhuan, and more than three hundred attending officials below them.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong reached Guide, the cavalry marshal Pucha Guannu rose in mutiny and killed Left Vice Councillor Li Xi, Participating Councillor Shizhan Nuluhuan, and more than three hundred officials in their train.

sentences.zh: 倉皇之際，哀宗不得已，以官奴權參知政事，既為所制，含恨欲誅之未能也。

translations.literal: In the emergency Aizong had no choice but to make Guannu acting participating councillor; once under his control, he harbored hatred and wished to execute him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis Aizong had no choice but to make Guannu acting participating councillor. Once he was under Guannu's control, he nursed hatred and wished to kill him but could not.

sentences.zh: 及官奴往亳州，珪陰與奉禦吾古孫愛實、納蘭忔答，護衛女奚烈完出、范陳僧、王山兒等謀誅之。

translations.literal: When Guannu went to Bo Prefecture, Gui secretly plotted with the palace attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Geda, the guardswoman Xilie Wanchu, Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, and others to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu went to Bo Prefecture, Gui secretly joined the palace attendant Wugusun Aishi, Nalan Geda, the guardswoman Xilie Wanchu, Fan Chenseng, Wang Shan'er, and others in a plot to kill him.

sentences.zh: 官奴自亳還，哀宗禦臨漪亭，召參政張天綱及官奴議事。

translations.literal: When Guannu returned from Bo, Aizong held court at the Yi Pavilion and summoned Participating Councillor Zhang Tiangang and Guannu to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guannu returned from Bo, Aizong held audience at the Yi Pavilion and summoned Participating Councillor Zhang Tiangang and Guannu to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 官奴入見，珪等即從旁殺之，及其党阿裏合、白進、習顯。

translations.literal: When Guannu entered for audience, Gui and the others immediately killed him from the side, along with his partisans Alihe, Bai Jin, and Xi Xian.
translations.idiomatic: As Guannu entered for audience, Gui and the others struck him down on the spot, along with his followers Alihe, Bai Jin, and Xi Xian.

sentences.zh: 及蔡城破，哀宗自縊于幽蘭軒，珪與完顏斜烈、焦春和等皆從死。

translations.literal: When Cai Prefecture city fell, Aizong hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion; Gui, Wanyan Xielie, Jiao Chunhe, and others all followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai city fell, Aizong hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion. Gui, Wanyan Xielie, Jiao Chunhe, and others died with him.

sentences.zh: 潘守恆

translations.literal: Pan Shouheng
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shouheng

sentences.zh: 有潘守恆者亦內侍也，素稱知書，南遷後規益甚多。

translations.literal: There was also Pan Shouheng, an inner attendant, long reputed learned; after the move south his remonstrances and benefits were many.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Pan Shouheng, an inner attendant long known for learning. After the court moved south, his counsel proved of great benefit again and again.

sentences.zh: 及哀宗自蒲城走歸德，道次民家，守恆進櫛，曰：「願陛下還宮之日無忘此草廬中，更加儉素，以濟大業。

translations.literal: When Aizong fled from Pucheng to Guide and stopped at a commoner's house on the way, Shouheng presented a comb and said: 'May Your Majesty on the day you return to the palace not forget this thatched hut, and be still more frugal and plain to accomplish the great enterprise.'
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong fled from Pucheng toward Guide and lodged at a farmer's house along the road, Shouheng brought him a comb and said, "When Your Majesty returns to the palace, do not forget this thatched hut. Be still more frugal and plain, that the great enterprise may yet be saved."

sentences.zh: 」上聞其言，淒惋咨嗟久之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor heard his words and mourned and sighed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard him and mourned and sighed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 太史公敘九流，述《日者》、《龜策》、《扁鵲倉公列傳》。

translations.literal: Grand Historian Sima Qian arranged the Nine Schools and composed the 'Biographies of the Day Diviners,' 'Tortoise and Yarrow,' and 'Bian Que and Lord Cang.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Historian Sima Qian surveyed the Nine Schools and wrote the biographies of day-diviners, tortoise-and-yarrow specialists, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang.

sentences.zh: 劉歆校中秘書，以術數、方伎載之《七略》。

translations.literal: Liu Xin collated the imperial secretariat books and placed numerology and technical arts in the Seven Summaries.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin collated the imperial library and placed numerology and the technical arts in his Seven Summaries.

sentences.zh: 後世史官作《方伎傳》，蓋祖其意焉。

translations.literal: Later dynasties' historians composed 'Biographies of Technical Masters,' broadly following his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians wrote biographies of technical masters in the same spirit.

sentences.zh: 或曰《素問》、《內經》言天道消長、氣運贏縮，假醫術，托岐黃，以傳其秘奧耳。

translations.literal: Some say the Plain Questions and Inner Canon speak of the waxing and waning of Heaven's Way and the surplus and deficit of vital breath, borrowing medicine and entrusting it to Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor merely to transmit secret profundities.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that the Plain Questions and Inner Canon really speak of Heaven's waxing and waning and the ebb and flow of cosmic breath, using medicine and the names of Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor only as vehicles for hidden doctrine.

sentences.zh: 秦人至以《周易》列之卜筮，斯豈易言哉！

translations.literal: The people of Qin even classified the Book of Changes under divination — this is surely not easily spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: The Qin even filed the Book of Changes under divination — such matters are not lightly judged!

sentences.zh: 第古之為術，以吉凶導人而為善，後世術者，或以休咎導人為不善，古之為醫，以活人為功，後世醫者，或因以為利而誤殺人。

translations.literal: Only in antiquity those who practiced arts used fortune and misfortune to guide people toward good; later practitioners sometimes used omens to lead people toward evil. In antiquity physicians took saving lives as merit; later physicians sometimes pursued profit and by mistake killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity practitioners of the arts used omens to steer people toward good; later ones sometimes used fortune and misfortune to lead them astray. Ancient physicians measured their merit by lives saved; later ones sometimes chased profit and killed by mistake.

sentences.zh: 故為政於天下，雖方伎之事，亦必慎其所職掌，而務旌別其賢否焉。

translations.literal: Therefore in governing the realm, even in matters of technical arts one must be careful in what offices hold and strive to distinguish the worthy from the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever governs the realm must therefore be careful even over technical arts, distinguishing clearly between the worthy and the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 金世，如武禎、武亢之信而不誣，劉完素、張元素之治療通變，學其術者皆師尊之，不可不記雲。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, men such as Wu Zhen and Wu Kang were faithful and not deceitful, and Liu Wansu and Zhang Yuansu were versatile in treatment; all who studied their arts honored them as teachers — they cannot go unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin, men such as Wu Zhen and Wu Kang proved trustworthy and true, while Liu Wansu and Zhang Yuansu were masters of adaptive treatment. All who learned from them revered them as teachers — and they must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 劉完素

translations.literal: Liu Wansu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu

sentences.zh: 劉完素，字守真，河間人。

translations.literal: Liu Wansu, style Shouzhen, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu, styled Shouzhen, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇異人陳先生，以酒飲守真，大醉，及寤洞達醫術，若有授之者。

translations.literal: He once met the extraordinary man Master Chen, who made Shouzhen drink wine until very drunk; when he awoke he was thoroughly versed in medicine, as if something had been imparted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He once met a remarkable man, Master Chen, who plied him with wine until he was deeply drunk. When he woke, he understood medicine completely, as though it had been handed to him.

sentences.zh: 乃撰《運氣要旨論》、《精要宣明論》，慮庸醫或出妄說，又著《素問玄機原病式》，特舉二百八十八字，注二萬餘言。

translations.literal: He then composed Essentials of Circulating Qi and Clarifying the Essentials of the Subtle, fearing that mediocre physicians might put forth reckless doctrines; he also wrote Patterns of Disease from the Mysterious Mechanism of the Plain Questions, specially citing two hundred eighty-eight characters and annotating them with more than twenty thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of Circulating Qi and Clarifying the Essentials of the Subtle, fearing that mediocre physicians might spread reckless theories. He also wrote Patterns of Disease from the Mysterious Mechanism of the Plain Questions, taking two hundred eighty-eight key characters and adding more than twenty thousand words of commentary.

sentences.zh: 然好用涼劑，以降心火、益腎水為主。

translations.literal: Yet he was fond of using cooling drugs, chiefly to lower heart fire and supplement kidney water.
translations.idiomatic: He favored cooling medicines above all, chiefly to reduce heart fire and strengthen kidney water.

sentences.zh: 自號「通元處士」雲。

translations.literal: He styled himself 'Hermit Who Penetrates the Origin.'
translations.idiomatic: He took for himself the sobriquet "Hermit Who Penetrates the Origin."

sentences.zh: 張從正

translations.literal: Zhang Congzheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congzheng

sentences.zh: 張從正，字子和，睢州考城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Congzheng, style Zihe, was a man of Kaocheng in Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congzheng, styled Zihe, was from Kaocheng in Sui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 精於醫，貫穿《難》、《素》之學，其法宗劉守真，用藥多寒涼，然起疾救死多取效。

translations.literal: He was expert in medicine and thoroughly penetrated the learning of the Difficult Classic and Plain Questions; his method followed Liu Shouzhen, and his drugs were mostly cold and cool, yet in raising the sick and saving the dying he often achieved effect.
translations.idiomatic: A master physician, he had fully mastered the Difficult Classic and Plain Questions. His method followed Liu Shouzhen, and his prescriptions were mostly cooling, yet he often saved the gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 古醫書有《汗下吐法》，亦有不當汗者汗之則死，不當下者下之則死，不當吐者吐之則死，各有經絡脈理，世傳黃帝、岐伯所為書也。

translations.literal: Ancient medical books have the 'sweating, purging, and emetic method,' yet there are cases where one who should not be made to sweat dies if sweated, one who should not be purged dies if purged, and one who should not be made to vomit dies if vomited — each has its channels, collaterals, and pulse principles; the world transmits that these were books made by the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient medical texts teach the methods of sweating, purging, and emesis — yet the wrong patient sweated, purged, or vomited will die. Each case has its proper channels and pulse logic. Tradition attributes these books to the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo.

sentences.zh: 從正用之最精，號「張子和汗下吐法」。

translations.literal: Congzheng used them with greatest mastery and was styled 'Master Zihe's sweating, purging, and emetic method.'
translations.idiomatic: Congzheng wielded them with supreme skill and was known for "Master Zihe's method of sweating, purging, and emesis."

sentences.zh: 妄庸淺術習其方劑，不知察脈原病，往往殺人，此庸醫所以失其傳之過也。

translations.literal: Reckless, mediocre, shallow practitioners learned his formulas without knowing how to examine pulses and trace diseases to their origin, and often killed people — this is why mediocre physicians lost the transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre practitioners copied his formulas without learning to read the pulse or trace disease to its root, and often killed their patients. That is how the art was lost in the hands of poor physicians.

sentences.zh: 其所著有「六門、二法」之目，存於世雲。

translations.literal: His writings include the categories 'Six Gates' and 'Two Methods,' which survive in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works under the titles "Six Gates" and "Two Methods" still survive.

sentences.zh: 李慶嗣

translations.literal: Li Qingsi
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingsi

sentences.zh: 李慶嗣，洺人。

translations.literal: Li Qingsi was a man of Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qingsi was from Mo.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士不第，棄而學醫，讀《素問》諸書，洞曉其義。

translations.literal: In youth he took the jinshi examination and failed; he abandoned that path and studied medicine, reading the Plain Questions and related books until he thoroughly understood their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination in his youth, turned to medicine instead, and read the Plain Questions and related texts until he understood them through and through.

sentences.zh: 天德間，歲大疫，廣平尤甚，貧者往往闔門臥病。

translations.literal: During Tiande there was a great epidemic in the year; Guangping suffered especially, and among the poor whole households often lay sick.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era a great epidemic struck; Guangping suffered worst of all, and poor families often saw every member fall ill at once.

sentences.zh: 廣嗣攜藥與米分遺之，全活者眾。

translations.literal: Qingsi carried medicine and rice and distributed them; many were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsi went about distributing medicine and rice, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 慶嗣年八十餘，無疾而終。

translations.literal: Qingsi lived more than eighty years and died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsi lived past eighty and died without illness.

sentences.zh: 所著《傷寒纂類》四卷、《改證活人書》三卷、《傷寒論》三卷、《針經》一卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: His works — Collected Categories of Cold Damage in four juan, Revised Evidence for the Book That Saves Lives in three juan, Treatise on Cold Damage in three juan, and Classic of Acupuncture in one juan — are transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Categories of Cold Damage (four juan), Revised Evidence for the Book That Saves Lives (three juan), Treatise on Cold Damage (three juan), and Classic of Acupuncture (one juan) survive to this day.

sentences.zh: 紀天錫

translations.literal: Ji Tianxi
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tianxi

sentences.zh: 紀天錫，字齊卿，泰安人。

translations.literal: Ji Tianxi, style Qiqing, was a man of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tianxi, styled Qiqing, was from Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 早棄進士業，學醫，精於其技，遂以醫名世。

translations.literal: He early abandoned the jinshi career, studied medicine, became expert in the art, and thereby made his name in medicine throughout the world.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the path to jinshi early, took up medicine, mastered the art, and won fame as a physician.

sentences.zh: 集注《難經》五卷，大定十五年上其書，授醫學博士。

translations.literal: He compiled a commentary on the Difficult Classic in five juan; in the fifteenth year of Dading he presented his book and was appointed erudite of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a five-juan commentary on the Difficult Classic. In the fifteenth year of Dading (1175) he presented it to the throne and was appointed erudite of medicine.

sentences.zh: 張元素

translations.literal: Zhang Yuansu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuansu

sentences.zh: 張元素，字潔古，易州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuansu, style Jiegu, was a man of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuansu, styled Jiegu, was from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 八歲試童子舉。

translations.literal: At eight he took the childhood licentiate examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he sat for the childhood licentiate examination.

sentences.zh: 二十七試經義進士，犯廟諱下第。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he took the jinshi examination in classical exegesis and failed for violating taboo on the imperial temple name.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he took the jinshi examination in classical exegesis but failed for violating imperial name taboo.

sentences.zh: 乃去學醫，無所知名，夜夢有人用大斧長鑿鑿心開竅，納書數卷於其中，自是洞徹其術。

translations.literal: He then left to study medicine without any reputation; one night he dreamed that someone used a great axe and long chisel to bore open his heart and insert several scrolls of books, and from then on he thoroughly penetrated the art.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to medicine without any reputation at first. One night he dreamed that a man opened his breast with a great axe and long chisel and placed several scrolls inside. From that night he understood the art completely.

sentences.zh: 河間劉完素病傷寒八日，頭痛脈緊，嘔逆不食，不和所為。

translations.literal: Liu Wansu of Hejian fell ill with cold damage for eight days, with headache, tight pulse, vomiting, and inability to eat, and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wansu of Hejian had been ill with cold damage for eight days — headache, a tight pulse, vomiting, and no appetite — and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 元素往候，完素面壁不顧，元素曰：「何見待之卑如此哉。

translations.literal: Yuansu went to visit him; Wansu turned his face to the wall and paid no attention. Yuansu said: 'Why do you treat me with such low regard?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu went to call on him. Wansu turned to the wall and ignored him. Yuansu said, "Why do you treat me with such contempt?"

sentences.zh: 」既為診脈，謂之曰脈病云云，曰：「然。

translations.literal: ' After examining his pulse he told him such-and-such about the pulse and disease; Wansu said: 'Yes.'
translations.idiomatic: " After taking his pulse he described the condition in detail. Wansu said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」「初服某藥，用某味乎？

translations.literal: ' 'At first did you take such-and-such medicine, using such-and-such ingredient?'
translations.idiomatic: " "Did you first take such-and-such medicine, using such-and-such ingredient?"

translations.literal: ' He said: 'Yes.'
translations.idiomatic: " "Yes," he said.

sentences.zh: 」元素曰：「子誤矣。

translations.literal: ' Yuansu said: 'You are mistaken.'
translations.idiomatic: " Yuansu said, "You are wrong.

sentences.zh: 某味性寒，下降走太陰，陽亡汗不能出。

translations.literal: That ingredient's nature is cold; it descends and travels to greater yin, yang is lost and sweat cannot be released.
translations.idiomatic: That ingredient is cold in nature. It drives downward into greater yin, yang is depleted, and sweat cannot break forth.

sentences.zh: 今脈如此，當服某藥則效矣。

translations.literal: Now with the pulse like this, you should take such-and-such medicine and it will be effective.
translations.idiomatic: With the pulse as it is now, you should take such-and-such medicine and you will recover.

sentences.zh: 」完素大服，如其言遂愈，元素自此顯名。

translations.literal: ' Wansu was greatly convinced; following his words he recovered, and from then on Yuansu became famous.
translations.idiomatic: " Wansu was deeply impressed. He followed the prescription and recovered, and from that day Yuansu's name spread.

sentences.zh: 平素治病不用古方，其說曰：「運氣不齊，古今異軌，古方新病不相能也。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he treated illness without using ancient formulas; his doctrine said: 'Circulating qi is not uniform, ancient and modern follow different tracks — ancient formulas and new diseases cannot suit each other.'
translations.idiomatic: In practice he never used ancient formulas. His doctrine ran: "Circulating qi is never uniform; antiquity and the present follow different paths. Ancient formulas cannot meet new diseases."

sentences.zh: 」自為家法雲。

translations.literal: ' This he made his household method.
translations.idiomatic: " That became his school of medicine.

sentences.zh: 馬貴中

translations.literal: Ma Guizhong
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guizhong

sentences.zh: 馬貴中，天德中，為司天提點。

translations.literal: Ma Guizhong, during Tiande, served as supervisor of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era Ma Guizhong served as supervisor of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 與校書郎高守元奏天象災異忤旨，海陵皆杖之，黜貴中為大同府判官。

translations.literal: Together with the proofreader Gao Shouyuan he memorialized on celestial omens and disasters contrary to the emperor's wish; Hailing had them both beaten and demoted Guizhong to assistant magistrate of Datong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He and the proofreader Gao Shouyuan memorialized on celestial omens and disasters in a way that displeased the emperor. Hailing had them both beaten and demoted Guizhong to assistant magistrate of Datong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷司天監。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to be director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 正隆三年三月辛酉朔，日當食。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenglong, third month, on the xinyou day that was the new moon, the sun was due for an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenglong, on the new-moon day xinyou in the third month, a solar eclipse was due.

sentences.zh: 是日，候之不食，海陵謂貴中曰：「自今凡遇日食皆面奏，不須頒示內外。」

translations.literal: That day they waited and the eclipse did not occur. Hailing said to Guizhong: 'From now on, whenever an eclipse occurs, report it in person; there is no need to proclaim it within and without.'
translations.idiomatic: That day they waited, but the sun was not eclipsed. Hailing told Guizhong, "From now on, whenever an eclipse is due, report to me in person. Do not issue proclamations inside and outside the court."

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，問曰：「朕欲自將伐宋，天道何如？

translations.literal: When Hailing attacked Song he asked: 'I wish to lead the campaign against Song in person — what does Heaven's Way indicate?'
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing prepared to attack the Song, he asked, "I mean to lead the campaign against Song myself. What do the heavens portend?"

sentences.zh: 」貴中對曰：「去年十月甲戌，熒惑順入太微，至屏星，留、退、西出。

translations.literal: ' Guizhong replied: 'Last year, tenth month, jiaxu day, Mars entered Supreme Palace in proper motion, reached Screen Star, stayed, retreated, and went out to the west.'
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong answered, "Last year, in the tenth month on the jiaxu day, Mars entered the Supreme Palace in direct motion, reached Screen Star, halted, retreated, and emerged to the west."

sentences.zh: 《占書》，熒惑常以十月入太微庭，受制出伺無道之國。

translations.literal: According to the Books of Prognostication, Mars often enters the court of Supreme Palace in the tenth month, is constrained, emerges, and watches for states without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication texts say Mars often enters the court of the Supreme Palace in the tenth month, is constrained, emerges, and watches for states that have lost the Way.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太白晝見經天，占為兵喪、為不臣、為更主，又主有兵兵罷、無兵兵起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Venus appeared in daylight crossing the sky; prognostication reads it as armies and mourning, as disloyal ministers, as change of ruler, and also: if there are armies the armies cease, if there are no armies armies arise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Venus was seen in daylight crossing the heavens. The omens signify war and mourning, disloyal ministers, and change of ruler; they also mean that where armies exist they will disband, and where none exist they will arise.

sentences.zh: 」鎮戎軍地震大風，海陵以問，貴中對曰：「伏陰逼陽，所以震也。

translations.literal: ' At Zhenrong Army post there was an earthquake and great wind; Hailing asked about it and Guizhong replied: 'Yin lying hidden presses yang — that is why there is quaking.'
translations.idiomatic: " At Zhenrong Army post there was an earthquake and a great wind. Hailing asked about it, and Guizhong replied, "Hidden yin presses upon yang — that is why the earth quakes."

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「當震，大風何也？

translations.literal: ' He asked again: 'When there is quaking, why is there great wind?'
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again, "If the earth quakes, why is there a great wind?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「土失其性則地震，風為號令，人君命令嚴急，則有烈風及物之災。

translations.literal: ' He replied: 'When earth loses its nature there is earthquake; wind is command — when the ruler's commands are stern and urgent, there are fierce winds and disasters reaching things.'
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "When earth loses its proper nature, the ground quakes. Wind is command. When a ruler's orders grow harsh and urgent, fierce winds strike and disaster reaches all things."

sentences.zh: 」六年二月甲辰朔，日有暈珥戴背，海陵問：「近日天道何如？

translations.literal: ' In the sixth year, second month, jiachen day at new moon, the sun had halos, aureoles, caps, and backs. Hailing asked: 'What has Heaven's Way been like recently?'
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth year, on the new-moon day jiachen in the second month, the sun showed halos, aureoles, caps, and backs. Hailing asked, "What have the heavens shown of late?"

sentences.zh: 」貴中對曰：「前年八月二十九日，太白入太微右掖門，九月二日，至端門，九日，至左掖門出，並曆左右執法。

translations.literal: ' Guizhong replied: 'The year before last, eighth month, twenty-ninth day, Venus entered Supreme Palace's right side gate; ninth month, second day, reached the central gate; ninth day, reached the left side gate and went out — all passing through the left and right law-enforcers.'
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong answered, "The year before last, on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month, Venus entered the right side gate of the Supreme Palace. On the second day of the ninth month it reached the central gate; on the ninth it passed out through the left side gate, traversing the left and right law-enforcers throughout."

sentences.zh: 太微為天子南宮，太白兵將之象，其占，兵入天子之廷。

translations.literal: Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven's southern palace; Venus is the image of armies and generals; the prognostication is that armies enter the Son of Heaven's court.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Palace is the sovereign's southern palace. Venus is the sign of armies and generals. The omen reads: armies enter the Son of Heaven's court.

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「今將征伐而兵將出入太微，正其事也。

translations.literal: ' Hailing said: 'Now I am about to campaign, and armies and generals entering and leaving Supreme Palace — that fits the affair exactly.'
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "I am about to campaign, and armies and generals passing in and out of the Supreme Palace — that suits the occasion exactly."

sentences.zh: 」貴中又曰；

translations.literal: ' Guizhong also said:
translations.idiomatic: " Guizhong added,

sentences.zh: 「當端門而出，其占為受制，曆左右執法為受事，此當有出使者，或為兵，或為賊。

translations.literal: 'When it went out at the central gate, the prognostication is being constrained; passing through the left and right law-enforcers means receiving affairs — there should be envoys going out, whether as armies or as bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: "When it passed out at the central gate, the omen was one of constraint. Passing the left and right law-enforcers means receiving commissions. Envoys will go forth — whether as armies or as rebels."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「兵興之際，小盜固不能無也。

translations.literal: ' Hailing said: 'When armies rise, small bandits surely cannot be absent.'
translations.idiomatic: " Hailing said, "When armies march, petty bandits are bound to appear."

sentences.zh: 」及被害於揚州，貴中之言皆驗。

translations.literal: ' When he met death at Yangzhou, all of Guizhong's words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was killed at Yangzhou, every word of Guizhong's proved true.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，世宗擊球于常武殿，貴中上疏諫曰：「陛下為天下主，守宗廟社稷之重，圍獵擊球皆危事也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading, Emperor Shizong played cuju at the Ever Martial Hall; Guizhong submitted a memorial remonstrating: 'Your Majesty is lord of all under Heaven, guarding the weight of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain — hunting and cuju are all dangerous affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading (1168), Emperor Shizong played cuju at the Ever Martial Hall. Guizhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Your Majesty is lord of all under Heaven, charged with the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. Hunting and cuju are dangerous pursuits."

sentences.zh: 前日皇太子墜馬，可以為戒，臣願一切罷之。

translations.literal: The other day the crown prince fell from his horse — that may serve as a warning; your servant wishes that all such activities be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince fell from his horse the other day. Let that be a warning. Your servant begs that all such pastimes be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「祖宗以武定天下，豈以承平遽忘之邪。

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'Our ancestors settled the realm by arms — how could we in a time of peace suddenly forget that?'
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Our ancestors settled the realm by force of arms. How could we forget that now, in a time of peace?"

sentences.zh: 皇統嘗罷此事，當時之人皆以為非，朕所親見，故示天下以習武耳。」

translations.literal: During Huangtong this matter was once abolished, and people of that time all thought it wrong — I saw it with my own eyes, and therefore show the realm military training, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangtong this practice was once abandoned, and everyone at the time thought it a mistake. I saw it myself. I keep these exercises only to show the realm that we still train for war."

sentences.zh: 十年十一月，皇太子生日，世宗宴百官於東宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the tenth year, on the crown prince's birthday, Shizong feasted the hundred officials at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the tenth year, on the crown prince's birthday, Shizong gave a feast for the officials at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上飲歡甚，貴中被酒，前跪欲言事，錯亂失次，上不之罪，但令扶出。

translations.literal: The emperor drank with great joy; Guizhong was drunk on wine, came forward kneeling wishing to speak on affairs, became confused and lost order; the emperor did not punish him but only ordered him helped out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank freely. Guizhong, drunk, knelt forward to speak on some matter, grew confused, and lost all decorum. The emperor did not punish him but had him helped out.

sentences.zh: 武禎，宿州臨渙人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhen was a man of Linhuan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhen was from Linhuan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖官太史，靖康後業農，後畫界屬金。

translations.literal: His grandfather had been a grand astrologer; after Jingkang he took up farming, and later when boundaries were drawn his land fell under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as grand astrologer. After the Jingkang disaster the family turned to farming, and when boundaries were redrawn their land fell under Jin rule.

sentences.zh: 禎深數學。

translations.literal: Zhen was deeply versed in numerology.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was deeply versed in numerology and divination.

sentences.zh: 貞祐間，行樞密院僕散安貞聞其名，召至徐州，以上客禮之，每出師必資焉。

translations.literal: During Zhenyou, the acting Bureau of Military Affairs Pusan Anzhen heard his name, summoned him to Xuzhou, treated him with guest-of-honor ceremony, and whenever he took the field relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyou, Pusan Anzhen of the acting Bureau of Military Affairs heard of him, summoned him to Xuzhou, and treated him as an honored guest. On every campaign he consulted him.

sentences.zh: 其占如響。

translations.literal: His prognostications were like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: His prognostications proved as sure as an echo.

sentences.zh: 正大初，征至汴京，待詔東華門。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda he was summoned to Bianjing and awaited imperial orders at the Donghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengda he was summoned to Bianjing and waited at the Donghua Gate for imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 其友王鉉問禎曰：「朝廷若問國祚修短，子何以對？

translations.literal: His friend Wang Xuan asked Zhen: 'If the court asks about the length of the dynasty's fate, how will you answer?'
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wang Xuan asked Zhen, "If the court asks how long the dynasty will endure, what will you say?"

sentences.zh: 」禎曰：「當以實告之，但更言周過其曆，秦不及期，亦在修德耳。

translations.literal: ' Zhen said: 'I should tell the truth, but add only that Zhou exceeded its allotted span, Qin fell short of its term — it all lies in cultivating virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen said, "I must speak the truth — but add that Zhou outlasted its allotted span while Qin fell short of its term. In the end it comes down to cultivating virtue."

sentences.zh: 」時久旱祈禱不應，朝廷為憂，禎忽謂鉉曰：「足下今日早歸，恐為雨阻。

translations.literal: ' At that time there had been long drought and prayers brought no response; the court was worried. Zhen suddenly said to Xuan: 'Sir, return home early today — I fear rain may block your way.'
translations.idiomatic: " There had been a long drought and prayers had brought no rain; the court was deeply worried. Zhen suddenly told Xuan, "Go home early today — I fear the rain may block your way."

sentences.zh: 」鉉曰：「萬里無雲，赤日如此，安得有雨？

translations.literal: ' Xuan said: 'For ten thousand li there is not a cloud; the red sun is like this — how could there be rain?'
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "Not a cloud for a thousand li, and the sun blazing down — how could there be rain?"

sentences.zh: 」禎笑曰：「若是，則天不誠也。

translations.literal: ' Zhen laughed and said: 'If that is so, then Heaven is not sincere.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen laughed. "If that were so, Heaven would not be sincere."

sentences.zh: 天何嘗不誠。

translations.literal: How could Heaven ever be insincere?
translations.idiomatic: When has Heaven ever been insincere?

sentences.zh: 」既而東南有雲氣，須臾蔽天，平地雨注二尺，眾皆驚歎。

translations.literal: ' Soon clouds arose in the southeast; in a moment they covered the sky, and on level ground rain poured two feet deep; all were startled and exclaimed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon clouds rose in the southeast. In a moment they blotted out the sky, and two feet of rain fell on level ground. Everyone marveled.

sentences.zh: 尋除司天臺管勾。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed registrar of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed registrar of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 子 亢

translations.literal: His son Kang
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang

sentences.zh: 子亢，寡言笑，不妄交。

translations.literal: His son Kang spoke little and laughed little, and did not associate rashly.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang spoke little, laughed little, and made friends cautiously.

sentences.zh: 嘗與一學生終日相對，握籌布畫，目炯炯若有所營，見者莫測也。

translations.literal: He once sat facing a student all day long, holding counting rods and laying out diagrams, eyes bright as if engaged in some design — those who saw him could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: He once sat facing a student all day, counting rods in hand and charts spread before him, eyes bright as though plotting some design. No one who saw him could guess his purpose.

sentences.zh: 哀宗至蔡州，右丞完顏仲德薦其術。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aizong reached Cai Prefecture, Right Vice Councillor Wanyan Zhongde recommended his arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aizong reached Cai Prefecture, Right Vice Councillor Wanyan Zhongde recommended his arts.

sentences.zh: 召至，屏人與語，大悅，除司天長行，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: He was summoned; the emperor dismissed attendants and spoke with him, was greatly pleased, appointed him senior director of astronomy, and bestowed rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was summoned. The emperor dismissed his attendants and spoke with him alone, was greatly pleased, appointed him senior director of astronomy, and lavished rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：「比者有星變于周、楚之分，彗星起於大角西，掃軫之左軸，蓋除舊佈新之象。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: 'Recently there have been stellar changes in the Zhou and Chu divisions; a comet rose west of Great Horn, sweeping the left axle of Chariot — this is an image of removing the old and spreading the new.'
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Of late stars have changed in the Zhou and Chu divisions. A comet rose west of Great Horn and swept the left axle of Chariot — a sign of casting off the old and setting up the new."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「鄭、楚、週三分野當赤地千里，兵凶大起，王者不可居也。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'The Zheng, Chu, and Zhou divisions will see a thousand li of bare red earth; armies and calamity will rise greatly — a king cannot dwell there.'
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The Zheng, Chu, and Zhou divisions will see a thousand li laid waste. War and disaster will rise on every side. No king can remain there."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「蔡城有兵喪之兆，楚有亡國之征，三軍苦戰於西垣前後有日矣。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'Cai city has omens of armies and mourning; Chu has signs of a perishing state; the three armies have fought bitterly before the western wall for days now.'
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Cai city bears omens of war and mourning. Chu shows the signs of a dying state. Our three armies have fought bitterly before the western wall for days."

sentences.zh: 城壁傾頹，內無見糧，外無應兵，君臣數盡之年也。

translations.literal: The walls are crumbling; within there is no grain in sight; without there are no relieving armies — this is the year when ruler and ministers exhaust their allotted span.
translations.idiomatic: The walls are crumbling. Within there is no grain to be seen; without, no army will come to our aid. This is the year when sovereign and ministers reach the end of their allotted span.

sentences.zh: 」聞者悚然奪氣，哀宗惟嗟歎良久，不以此罪。

translations.literal: ' Those who heard were startled and lost their breath; Aizong only sighed for a long time and did not punish him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him were stricken and lost heart. Aizong only sighed for a long while and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 性頗倨傲，朝士以此非之。

translations.literal: His nature was rather arrogant, and court officials faulted him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather arrogant by nature, and court officials criticized him for it.

sentences.zh: 天興二年九月，蔡州被圍，亢奏曰：「十二月三日必攻城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Tianxing, when Cai Prefecture was besieged, Kang memorialized: 'On the third day of the twelfth month they will certainly attack the city.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Tianxing, when Cai Prefecture was under siege, Kang memorialized, "On the third day of the twelfth month the enemy will attack the city."

sentences.zh: 」及期果然。

translations.literal: ' When the day came it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: " When the day came, it happened exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 末帝問曰：「解圍當在何日？

translations.literal: The Last Emperor asked: 'On what day will the siege be lifted?'
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor asked, "When will the siege be lifted?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「明年正月十三日，城下無一人一騎矣。

translations.literal: ' He replied: 'On the thirteenth day of the first month next year there will not be a single man or horse beneath the walls.'
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "On the thirteenth day of the first month next year there will not be a single man or horse beneath the walls."

sentences.zh: 」帝不知其由，乃喜圍解有期，日但密計糧草，使可給至其日不闕者。

translations.literal: ' The emperor did not understand his meaning and therefore rejoiced that the siege would be lifted on a set day; day by day he secretly calculated grain and fodder so that supplies could last until that day without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not grasp his meaning and rejoiced that relief would come on a fixed day. Each day he secretly calculated grain and fodder so that supplies would last until then.

sentences.zh: 明年甲午正月十日，蔡州破，十三日，大元兵退。

translations.literal: The next year, jiawu year, tenth day of the first month, Cai Prefecture fell; on the thirteenth day the Great Yuan armies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the tenth day of the first month in the jiawu cycle, Cai Prefecture fell. On the thirteenth day the armies of the Great Yuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是日，亢赴水死雲。

translations.literal: On that day Kang went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Kang drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 李懋，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Li Mao — it is not known whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mao — no one knows where he came from.

sentences.zh: 有異術。

translations.literal: He possessed extraordinary arts.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed extraordinary arts.

sentences.zh: 正大間，遊京兆，行省完顏合達愛其術，與俱至汴京，薦于哀宗。

translations.literal: During Zhengda he traveled in Jingzhao; the regional command Wanyan Hedai admired his arts, went with him to Bianjing, and recommended him to Aizong.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengda he traveled in the Jingzhao region. The regional commander Wanyan Hedai admired his arts, accompanied him to Bianjing, and recommended him to Emperor Aizong.

sentences.zh: 遣近侍密問國運否泰，言無忌避。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a close attendant to ask him secretly about the dynasty's fortune, prosperity or decline; he spoke without taboo or evasion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a close attendant to ask him privately whether the dynasty would rise or fall. He spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 居之繁台寺，朝士日走問之，或能道隱事及吉凶之變，人以為神。

translations.literal: He lodged him at Fantai Temple; court officials daily hurried to question him, and he could sometimes speak of hidden affairs and changes of fortune and misfortune — people took him for divine.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged Mao at Fantai Temple. Court officials flocked to him daily. He could speak of hidden affairs and coming fortune or disaster, and people took him for a god.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其言太泄，遣使者殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked that his words were too revealing and sent an envoy to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disliked his indiscreet speech and sent an envoy to kill him.

sentences.zh: 使者乃持酒肴入寺，懋出迎，笑曰：「是矣。

translations.literal: The envoy then entered the temple bearing wine and food; Mao came out to welcome him, smiled, and said: 'This is it.'
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered the temple with wine and food. Mao came out to meet him, smiled, and said, "So it has come."

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: ' The envoy said: 'What do you mean?'
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」懋曰：「我數當盡今日，尚複何言。

translations.literal: ' Mao said: 'My allotted span ends today — what more is there to say?'
translations.idiomatic: " Mao said, "My allotted span ends today. What more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」遂索酒，痛飲就死。

translations.literal: ' He then asked for wine, drank deeply, and met death.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked for wine, drank deeply, and died.

sentences.zh: 胡德新

translations.literal: Hu Dexin
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dexin

sentences.zh: 胡德新，河北士族也。

translations.literal: Hu Dexin was of a gentry family of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dexin came from a gentry family of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 寓居南陽，往來宛、葉間，嗜酒落魄不羈，言禍福有奇驗。

translations.literal: He lodged in Nanyang and traveled between Wan and Ye, fond of wine, down-and-out and unrestrained; in speaking of fortune and misfortune he had strange verification.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Nanyang and traveled between Wan and Ye. He loved wine, lived freely, and paid little heed to convention. When he spoke of fortune and misfortune, his words proved uncannily true.

sentences.zh: 正大七年夏，與燕人王鉉邂逅於葉縣村落中。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Zhengda he met by chance Wang Xuan of Yan in a village of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year of Zhengda he met by chance Wang Xuan of Yan in a village of Ye County.

sentences.zh: 與鉉初不相識，坐中謬以兵官對，胡曰：「此公在吾法中當登科甲，何以謂之兵官。

translations.literal: He and Xuan did not know each other at first; those seated wrongly addressed him as a military officer. Hu said: 'This gentleman by my art should attain the highest civil rank — why call him a military officer?'
translations.idiomatic: They did not know each other at first. Someone at the gathering mistook Wang for a military officer. Hu said, "By my art this gentleman should win the highest civil honors. Why call him a soldier?"

sentences.zh: 」眾愕然，遂以實告。

translations.literal: ' The company was startled and thereupon told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: " The company was astonished and told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 二人相得甚歡，即命家人具雞酒以待，酒酣、舉大白相屬曰：「君此去事業甚遠，不必置問。

translations.literal: The two men took to each other with great delight; he immediately ordered his household to prepare chicken and wine to entertain him. When the wine was warm he raised a full cup and pledged him, saying: 'Your career from here will reach very far — there is no need to ask about it.'
translations.idiomatic: The two took to each other at once. Hu ordered chicken and wine prepared. When the wine had warmed him, he raised a full cup and pledged Wang: "Your career from here will go far — there is no need to ask about it.

sentences.zh: 某有所見，久不敢對人言，今欲告子。

translations.literal: I have something I have seen but long dared not speak of to others; now I wish to tell you.'
translations.idiomatic: I have seen something I have long dared not tell anyone. Now I wish to tell you."

sentences.zh: 」遂邀至野田，密謂曰：「某自去年來，行宛、葉道中，見往來者十且八九有死氣。

translations.literal: ' He then invited him to the open fields and said secretly: 'Since last year, traveling the roads between Wan and Ye, I have seen that nine or eight of every ten travelers bear the air of death.'
translations.idiomatic: He led Wang into the open fields and said in secret, "Since last year, traveling the roads between Wan and Ye, I have seen that eight or nine of every ten passersby bear the air of death."

sentences.zh: 今春至陳、許間，見其人亦有大半當死者。

translations.literal: This spring, reaching the region between Chen and Xu, I saw that among those people too more than half were due to die.
translations.idiomatic: This spring, in the region between Chen and Xu, I saw that more than half of the people there were likewise marked for death.

sentences.zh: 若吾目可用，則時事可知矣。

translations.literal: If my eyes can be trusted, then the times may be known.
translations.idiomatic: If my eyes can be trusted, the times are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 」鉉驚問應驗遲速，曰：「不過歲月間耳，某亦不逃此厄，請密志之。

translations.literal: ' Xuan asked in alarm how soon it would be verified; he said: 'It will be no more than within the months — I too shall not escape this calamity. Please record this in secret.'
translations.idiomatic: " Wang asked in alarm how soon this would come to pass. Hu said, "No more than a year. I shall not escape this calamity either. Please keep this secret."

sentences.zh: 」明年，大元兵由金、房入，取峭石灘渡漢，所過廬舍蕭然，胡亦舉家及難，其精驗如此。

translations.literal: ' The next year the Great Yuan armies entered by way of Jin and Fang, crossed the Han at Qiaoshi Ford, and wherever they passed dwellings stood desolate; Hu's whole household also met disaster — such was the strange verification of his art.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year the armies of the Great Yuan entered through Jin and Fang, crossed the Han at Qiaoshi Ford, and laid waste to every dwelling in their path. Hu's whole household perished as well. Such was the uncanny truth of his art.
